heading: INT. CHURCH BELL TOWER - OBSERVATION POST - DAY (1944)

units.text: INT. CHURCH BELL TOWER - OBSERVATION POST - DAY (1944)
A cramped stone chamber at the top of a ruined bell tower.
The great bell is gone, its beam splintered.
Sunlight and dust pour through a shell hole in the east wall.
Sandbags ring a rough table covered with maps, a field telephone, and a pair of binoculars on a leather strap.
SERGEANT AUGUSTINE MBEKI, 40s, lean and weathered, a helmet tilted back, studies the valley through the shell hole with the binoculars.
CORPORAL WILHELMINA DAHL, 20s, a signaler, sits cross-legged on the floor, a radio headset around her neck, cleaning a rifle.
PRIVATE ANSELMO OKRZEJA, 19, freckled, anxious, hugs a canteen against his chest in the corner.
Nobody talks.
The wind moves a corner of the map.
Far below, a dog barks once and is silent.
Movement on the south road. Two trucks. Maybe three.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: Ours or theirs?
units.name: DAHL

units.text: Can't tell yet.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: They're all gray at this distance.
units.name: DAHL

units.text: She sets the rifle across her knees and reaches for the field telephone.
Okrzeja stands too quickly and bumps the table.
The binoculars slide and Mbeki catches them against his chest without looking.
Sorry, Sergeant.
units.name: OKRZEJA

units.text: Sit down, Private. Drink your water.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: It's empty.
units.name: OKRZEJA

units.text: Then hold it.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: Okrzeja sits.
He holds the canteen against his chest like a child holds a doll.
Mbeki lowers the binoculars and rubs the bridge of his nose.
Post Seven to Battalion. Do you copy?
units.name: DAHL

units.text: The phone crackles.
Nothing.
She tries again, tapping the cradle.
Line's dead.
units.name: DAHL

units.text: Try the radio.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: Radio is on a different battery.
units.name: DAHL

units.text: Then change the battery.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: We don't have another battery.
units.name: DAHL

units.text: Mbeki sets the binoculars down.
For the first time, he looks tired.
He takes a cigarette out of his breast pocket, looks at it, puts it back.
All right. Everyone listen.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: Dahl and Okrzeja turn.
If those trucks are ours, they'll stop at the crossroads and unload. If they're theirs, they'll come straight up. We will know in ten minutes. Until then, we do nothing.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: Nothing?
units.name: OKRZEJA

units.text: We sit. We breathe. We stay quiet.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: And if they're theirs?
units.name: OKRZEJA

units.text: Then we start doing something.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: Dahl wipes her hands on her trousers, checks the bolt on her rifle, and moves to the shell hole beside the sergeant.
Okrzeja crawls forward on hands and knees and wedges himself on the other side.
The three of them look out together, shoulder to shoulder, at the winding white road.
Dust rises.
A truck appears around the bend, then another.
They crawl along the ridge at walking pace.
Sergeant, can you read the markings?
units.name: DAHL

units.text: Not yet.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: Is that a flag?
units.name: OKRZEJA

units.text: It's a tarp.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: The lead truck slows at the crossroads.
The second slows behind it.
For a long moment everything is still.
The engines idle.
Then, from the back of the lead truck, a figure jumps down and waves a green cloth over his head.
Green.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: Ours.
units.name: DAHL

units.text: Oh, thank God.
units.name: OKRZEJA

units.text: Mbeki lowers the binoculars.
Dahl lets her head sag against the sandbag.
Okrzeja laughs, a wet, hiccupping laugh, and puts the empty canteen to his lips.
He tips it back, remembers it is empty, and laughs again.
Corporal. Hang up the phone.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: It was dead, Sergeant.
units.name: DAHL

units.text: I know. Hang it up anyway.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: She does.
Mbeki steps back from the hole, lights the cigarette this time, and lets the smoke curl up through the broken ceiling.
A hawk drifts across the sun.
The wind picks up the corner of the map again, and nobody bothers to hold it down.
Two more days.
units.name: DAHL

units.text: What?
units.name: OKRZEJA

units.text: Nothing. I'm counting.
units.name: DAHL
